sections.html:
The Columbus County Tax Office is at 810 Pinckney Street, Whiteville, with a public lobby open from half past eight to five. Call 910-640-6635, or write to P.O. Box 1468, Whiteville, NC 28472.

You can pay by mail, phone, online, dropbox or in person, with cash, check or credit card. The collections page has the details. Online payments go through columbus.webtaxpay.com, and the phone line is 877-768-4775.

The office collects for more than the county. It also bills for the City of Whiteville and the towns of Fair Bluff, Sandyfield, Boardman, Brunswick, Cerro Gordo, Bolton, Chadbourn, Tabor City and Lake Waccamaw. If you cannot find an old balance for one of those towns, call town hall.

sections.h2: Property tax rate and fire districts
sections.html:
The county rate is $0.805 per $100 of assessed valuation for fiscal year 2026-2027, and all of it goes to the General Fund. Commissioners adopted the budget ordinance on June 1, 2026. It rests on an estimated total valuation of $4,010,748,958 and a collection rate of 97.72 percent, and it allows discounts for early payment. Two school systems, Columbus County Schools and Whiteville City Schools, serve the county. A special fire tax by district is added on top of the county rate.

Ask the tax office which fire district your parcel is in and whether a city or town levy also applies.

Columbus County last revalued in 2021, and the next revaluation is set for 2029. Property tax revenue stays relatively flat outside revaluation years, at roughly $30 million a year for the county.

If you sell before 2029, expect the assessed value to date from 2021. Median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 was $146,000. If your own figure looks far from that, ask the appraisal staff how your parcel was valued.

The county has about 50,487 residents and 23,724 housing units, and owners live in 71.1 percent of homes.

Taxes are due September 1, and January 5 is the last day before delinquency. Amounts quoted are good through the last day of the month, and interest of three-fourths of 1 percent accrues on the first day of each month on delinquent taxes. State law adds a 2 percent charge from January 6 to February 1 under G.S. 105-360. Mailed payments count as received on the USPS postmark date.

After a parcel has been advertised for sale, only certified funds are accepted to redeem it. Once the court confirms a sale, North Carolina allows no redemption. To learn whether a property is in tax foreclosure, ask the tax collector's office directly.

sections.h2: How a tax foreclosure sale works
sections.html:
Sales take place outside the main entrance of the Columbus County Courthouse unless the weather is bad. The notice posted at the courthouse and printed in the newspaper controls; the foreclosures page is only an informal list of answers.

  • The high bidder pays a deposit of 20 percent of the bid or $750, whichever is greater. On sales over $5,000, a $1,000 cash deposit is due at once, with the rest within two business days.
  • Every bid is open to a 10-day upset period. Upset bids are filed through the Clerk of Court with a 5 percent or $750 deposit, whichever is greater.
  • After the upset period ends and the sale is confirmed, the last high bidder has three days to pay the balance to the commissioner.
  • The owner keeps the property until a new deed is recorded and may redeem until the court confirms the sale.

Upset bid amounts are found through the NC eCourts portal using the full file number, and the bid form is AOC-CV-414. The clerk will not answer upset bid questions by phone or fill out the form for you.

The county posts an application for the elderly and disabled exclusion, and the state also offers a disabled-veteran exclusion and a circuit breaker deferral. Filing runs from January 1 to June 1, and each owner may use one program.

  • County application (2025 tax year): household income at or under $37,900, age 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled on January 1, and a permanent residence titled in the applicant's exact name.
  • 2026 tax year: the income ceiling rises to $38,800, and the excluded amount is the larger of $25,000 or half the appraised value.
  • Owners with a disabled-veteran designation: $45,000 of appraised value is excluded, with no age or income test, on Form NCDVA-9.
  • Circuit breaker: tax is limited to 4 percent of income up to the limit and 5 percent above it, up to 150 percent of the limit.

The county asks for the prior year's income tax statement, an SSA-1099, a doctor's certification for applicants under 65, and a death certificate where a spouse has died and the deed was not corrected. Applications are denied if they are incomplete, if the name on the deed differs from the application, or if they miss the deadline. An approved elderly or disabled application does not have to be repeated each year unless household circumstances or income change. A circuit breaker application is filed anew every year.

Start with the appraisal staff. If that fails, the next forum is the county's equalization board, which by state law is the board of commissioners unless a special board is created. Ask who sits on Columbus County's.

The board opens its session between the first Monday in April and the first Monday in May. In an ordinary year it finishes by the third Monday after its first meeting and generally cannot sit past July 1. A hearing request, in writing or in person, must arrive before adjournment, or within 15 days of a late-mailed notice. Rulings are mailed within 30 days.

Beyond the board is the Property Tax Commission, with a 30-day filing window that runs from the board's mailing date. Vehicles, equipment and other personal property are handled by separate staff at the tax office.

State law (Session Law 2018-113 and G.S. 106-741) requires land records to carry a notice for anyone researching title. It flags a tract within one-half mile of a poultry, swine or dairy qualifying farm or a voluntary agricultural district, or within 600 feet of any other qualifying farm. The county has about 54 people per square mile on 938.12 square miles of land, so farm and rural parcels are common and the notice is worth reading.

The tax office page also lists staff for the solid waste trash user fee and for senior citizen exemptions. Before closing, ask whether any trash fee is attached to your parcel.

If a farm house, an inherited tract or a back-tax parcel is hard to sell the usual way, our North Carolina page explains a cash sale.

faqs.q: What is the Columbus County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The fiscal year 2026-2027 county rate is $0.805 per $100 of assessed value. Fire district taxes range from 0.06 to 0.12 per $100, and city or town taxes are billed separately.

faqs.q: When are Columbus County property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1. January 5 is the last day to pay before interest begins, which then builds at three-fourths of 1 percent a month after the initial January 6 charge.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Columbus County property taxes in person?
faqs.a: At the Columbus County Tax Office, 810 Pinckney Street, Whiteville, from half past eight until five. You can also pay by mail, by phone at 877-768-4775, online or at the dropbox.

faqs.q: When is the next Columbus County revaluation?
Can I stop a Columbus County tax foreclosure?
faqs.a: An owner can redeem until the court confirms the sale, by paying the taxes, interest and costs. After advertising, the county takes certified funds only.
